comments.author: Alex Kim
comments.body: Auth service compare is nameId === user.email. Planning to normalize with email domain rules and add a case-variant fixture.

content.text: Auth service compare is nameId === user.email. Planning to normalize with email domain rules and add a case-variant fixture.

SSO login fails when the IdP assertion NameID email has a mixed-case domain (e.g. User@Example.COM) while the Nimbus user record stores the domain lowercased (user@example.com). Local-part case handling is already fine; only the domain comparison breaks.

Authentication should succeed when the case-insensitive email matches a provisioned user. Today the SSO callback does an exact string match on the full NameID against users.email, returning No user matched this identity for mixed-case domains.

Enterprise IdPs often emit domains in the case registered in their directory. Normalizing both sides with a domain-lowercase (RFC 5321) compare before lookup should allow login without forcing customers to re-provision.
